subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should `current` and `session:*` cron jobs persist an explicit announce delivery object at creation, or should they continue using runtime-inferred delivery so persistent-session ownership remains distinct from `isolated` jobs?
rationale: Both paths can produce an announcement, but they create different persisted state and may select different delivery ownership; repository history and docs do not establish that materializing the implicit default is intended.

options.title: Keep Runtime Resolution
options.body: Retain the current stored shape and require a real failing cron transcript before changing delivery persistence or ownership.

options.title: Persist Announce Defaults
options.body: Approve the new stored default only with explicit compatibility review, upgrade coverage, and exact-head live proof for both persistent target forms.

options.title: Close Without Change
options.body: Close the PR if a current-main live run confirms that runtime delivery already solves the reported user problem.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime Resolution
recommendation.body: Retain the current stored shape and require a real failing cron transcript before changing delivery persistence or ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged session-target contract and its delivery implications were authored and landed through this owner’s work.
